newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES' LAFONTAINE CLEARED BY DOCTORS TO PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES' LAFONTAINE CLEARED BY DOCTORS TO PRACTICE.

text.p: Buffalo Sabres star centre Pat LaFontaine, who has not played since November 7 due to post-concussion syndrome, has been cleared to begin practicing with the team.
LaFontaine, whose condition has forced him to consider retirement, has not yet received clearance to return to active status and can only participate in non-contact drills, the team said.

The Sabres, in a press release, called LaFontaine's return to the ice "an important next step in the rehabilitation process." But the Buffalo captain will remain on the injured reserve list pending future medical evaluations.
LaFontaine suffered his most recent concussion from an elbow to the head in an October 17 game against Pittsburgh and last played in a November 7 loss to Philadelphia.
He complained of memory loss and dizzy spells early on, but doctors have been pleased by his recent improvement.
The 31-year-old LaFontaine, one of the best American-born players in NHL history, had suffered severe concussions previously in his career.
The 5-foot-10 (1.78 m), 180-pound (81.6 kg) centre led the Sabres with 40 goals and 91 points last season.
LaFontaine, who began his NHL career in 1984 with the New York Islanders, has 445 goals and 506 assists in 798 regular season games.
